note: The versions CI actually runs. `minimum` is what the project still supports; `verified` is what the ubuntu-24.04 runner ships and what .devcontainer/Dockerfile installs. check_toolchain.py fails when a tool that is present on the host is older than its minimum, and skips tools that are absent (a host job has no ARM toolchain).
why_clang_format_is_special: clang-format changes its output between major versions. Formatting a tree with 14 and checking it with 18 produces failures that are not real. Keep the local major version equal to CI's.

arm-none-eabi.gate: Cortex-M0/M4 cross build (the tools themselves are declared above); the file still lives under .github/ until #125 moves startup/link/toolchain into the SoC packages

iar-arm.gate: IAR Cortex-M firmware (D25); needs iccarm plus a licence, so it is not installed in CI and is never required to be present

toolchain_note: Vendor toolchains are declared here so a product can name one and so a new toolchain file cannot be added without the manifest noticing: check_toolchain.py fails when a *.cmake under `toolchain_dirs` is not declared, or when a declared file does not exist. They are never *required* to be installed - absence is skipped, exactly like the ARM toolchain on a host job.
